stem: After an unusually severe dryback, media pulls away from the container wall and irrigation water rapidly exits along the side while the root ball stays partly dry. What should be addressed first?
choices: Restore uniform wetting and correct preferential flow before assuming the crop needs a larger nutrient dose or irrigation event
Increase fertilizer concentration so the shrunken dry media absorbs irrigation more effectively during the next application and the root ball rehydrates without changing delivery
Reduce irrigation monitoring temporarily so the media can re-expand naturally before changing the delivery pattern
Treat rapid sidewall drainage as evidence that the whole root ball is saturated and maintain the existing irrigation event
rationale: Media shrinkage can create preferential flow paths that bypass part of the root zone. Re-establishing uniform wetting is more appropriate than assuming rapid drainage means complete rehydration.
